newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran's oil minister outlines foreign gas plans.
newsitem.headline: Iran's oil minister outlines foreign gas plans.

text.p: Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh said Tehran had given priority to developing gas links to Pakistan, India, Turkey and Armenia, the English-language Iran News paper reported on Thursday.
"After the completion of the natural gas supply network inside Iran, we have some major projects in the drawing board for its supply abroad," Iran News quoted Aghazadeh as saying.
The report was carried by the official IRNA news agency.
Iran aims to pipe natural gas to Pakistan and India and signed a $23 billion long-term agreement with Turkey in August for supplies beginning end-1997 or early 1998.
"Pakistan, India, Armenia and Turkey are on the priority list, and in some cases we have already signed agreements," Aghazadeh said.
Work on the gas export pipeline to Turkey will start within three months, which would allow Turkey to buy three billion cubic metres of gas from Iran, rising to 10 billion in 2005, Aghazadeh said.
"The natural gas pipeline will tie the Iranian and Turkish nations together by a sincere rope of friendship," the paper quoted him as saying.
Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said his government would open a tender this month to build a pipeline that would carry Iranian gas under the 23-year agreement.
Talks on developing a pipeline to Pakistan and India have been hampered because of the high cost and political obstacles.
Aghazadeh told the paper that a technical committee had been appointed and that a project report would be available in a few months' time.

"According to the plan, 1.6 billion cubic feet of natural gas will be supplied to Pakistan every day," Aghazadeh said, adding that after the signing of the agreement it will take four years for Iran to supply the gas.
Iran holds the world's second largest gas reserves after Russia but export projects have taken a secondary role to expanding the country's domestic gas supply network.
